chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the sign of the Night of Pre-determination, so he said: Its sign is that its wind becomes fragrant; and if it is in cold weather, it becomes warm, and if it is in hot weather, it becomes cool, and thus it becomes pleasant.

He said: And I asked him about the Night of Pre-determination, so he said: The angels and the scribes descend therein to the lowest heaven, so they write what will be of the matters of the year and what will befall the servants. And His Command is Reserved for Him, and in it is the Desire. So He brings forward from it whatever He wills and delays from it whatever He wills, and He obliterates and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of the Night of Pre-determination (Laylat al-Qadr) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the dual nature of Laylat al-Qadr, combining sensory signs—such as fragrant air and moderated temperature—with its metaphysical role as the night of divine decree. It highlights the Shia understanding of *al-mahw wa al-isbat* (obliteration and confirmation), where angels record the year's events in the lowest heaven, subject to God's will and ultimately anchored in *Umm al-Kitab*. This reflects the interplay between fixed destiny and divine flexibility, a core concept in Shia eschatology and jurisprudence.
